name: Pete Aguilar

lean.basis: Democratic mayor of Redlands, California, and congressman since 2015; chair of the House Democratic Caucus since 2023.

office.title: Chair of the House Democratic Caucus (majority whip-designate for January 2027)

current_role: Chair of the House Democratic Caucus (since 2023); majority whip-designate for the Congress that opens January 3, 2027
summary: Pete Aguilar, a former mayor of Redlands, has represented an Inland Empire district of California in the House since 2015 and chaired the House Democratic Caucus since 2023, making him the highest-ranking Latino in Congress. He served on the January 6 select committee, and after Democrats won the House in November 2026 he was designated to become majority whip.

sources.title: House Democrats prepare to elect leaders for the new Congress — AJC (AP)

timeline.role: Member, House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack
Chair of the House Democratic Caucus

connections.name: Hakeem Jeffries
connections.description: Aguilar succeeded Jeffries as House Democratic Caucus chair in 2023 and serves in his leadership team.

connections.name: Nancy Pelosi
connections.description: Aguilar was vice chair of the House Democratic Caucus (2021–2023) under Speaker Pelosi, and she named him to the January 6 select committee.

connections.name: Donald Trump
connections.description: As a member of the January 6 select committee Aguilar led a 2022 hearing on Trump's pressure on Mike Pence to overturn the election; he was among the committee members Biden pre-emptively pardoned in January 2025.

connections.name: Joe Biden
connections.description: Biden pre-emptively pardoned the members of the January 6 select committee, including Aguilar, in January 2025.

connections.name: Katherine Clark
connections.description: Aguilar lost the 2018 race for House Democratic Caucus vice chair to Clark, 90–144.

sources.title: Clark wins spot as Dem caucus vice chair — The Hill

connections.name: Katherine Clark
connections.description: Fellow members of the House Democratic leadership under Jeffries since 2023 (caucus chair and whip).
